items.headline: Jharkhand Assembly passes resolution against SIR
items.claim: News Arena India reported that the Jharkhand Assembly passed a resolution opposing the SIR, moved by Parliamentary Affairs Minister Radhakrishna Kishore on behalf of the INDIA bloc, and that the Speaker declared it passed without a vote while the BJP opposed it.
items.quote: A resolution opposing the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls was passed in the Jharkhand assembly on Tuesday. The resolution was introduced by Parliamentary Affairs Minister Radhakrishna Kishore, who alleged that the SIR was an attempt to weaken parliamentary democracy and disenfranchise the poor and downtrodden, and was designed to directly benefit the central ruling party.

items.headline: Kerala Assembly passes unanimous resolution against SIR
items.claim: The Siasat Daily, carrying a PTI report, said the Kerala Assembly unanimously passed a resolution moved by Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan against the SIR in the state, with the Congress-led opposition backing it.
items.quote: Kerala Assembly on Monday unanimously passed a resolution against the Election Commission of India (ECI)’s move to carry out the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voters’ list in the state and urged the poll body to conduct the revision of voters’ list in a transparent manner.

items.headline: Tamil Nadu all-party meeting opposes Election Commission’s voter roll revision, to move Supreme Court
items.claim: The News Minute reported that an all-party meeting chaired by Chief Minister M.K. Stalin, attended by nearly 50 parties, resolved to approach the Supreme Court against the SIR in Tamil Nadu. The AIADMK and the BJP were not invited and several other parties stayed away.
items.quote: In Tamil Nadu, an all-party meeting on November 2 by the ruling Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) and chaired by Chief Minister MK Stalin resolved to approach the Supreme Court of India against the Election Commission’s controversial Special Intensive Revision (SIR) in the state ahead of the 2026 Assembly elections.

items.headline: Bandh Against SIR By INDIA Alliance Throws Life Out Of Gear In Bihar
items.claim: ETV Bharat reported that a Bihar bandh called by the INDIA bloc parties against the SIR disrupted life across much of the state, with Rahul Gandhi and Tejashwi Yadav taking part.
items.quote: Patna: The Bihar Bandh called by parties of INDIA Alliance to protest against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) before the Assembly elections, threw life out of gear in most parts of the state.

items.headline: Assembly Protest Bihar: Anti-SIR Demonstrations Disrupt Monsoon Session Opening Day
items.claim: Deccan Herald, carrying a PTI report, said opposition members protested against the SIR inside the Bihar Assembly on the first day of its monsoon session, with CPI(ML) Liberation legislators wearing black.
items.quote: Patna: Protests against special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Bihar rocked the state assembly on the inaugural day of the monsoon session on Monday.

items.headline: Sonia, Kharge, Rahul, Akhilesh Join Opposition Leaders In Protest Against SIR
items.claim: ETV Bharat reported that INDIA bloc MPs protested at the Makar Dwar of Parliament against the Bihar SIR for a fifth day running and demanded that it be rolled back.
items.quote: Several MPs of the INDIA bloc parties, including Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge and Congress parliamentary party chairperson Sonia Gandhi, protested in the Parliament House complex on Monday against the Election Commission's voter roll revision in Bihar, and demanded its rollback.

items.headline: Police Stop March of 300 Opposition MPs Against Bihar SIR, Detain Lawmakers
items.claim: The Wire reported that Delhi Police detained opposition MPs, among them Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi, when their march from Parliament to the Election Commission against the Bihar SIR was stopped, and that they were released in the afternoon.
items.quote: Opposition MPs including leaders of opposition in the Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha – Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi – were detained by Delhi Police today (August 11) after they were stopped during their protest march against the ‘special intensive revision’ of the voter rolls in Bihar.
items.response: The Wire reported that the Commission had written to Jairam Ramesh the day before asking for the names of 30 members for a meeting “due to limitation of space”.

items.headline: Rahul Gandhi Kicks Off 'Vote Adhikar Yatra' In Bihar To 'Protect' Electoral Rights
items.claim: ETV Bharat reported that Rahul Gandhi began a 16-day Vote Adhikar Yatra from Sasaram against the SIR in Bihar, due to end with a rally in Patna on 1 September. The Congress leader alleged that the SIR was being done to steal votes.
items.quote: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi began his ‘Vote Adhikar Yatra’ from Sasaram on Sunday, protesting against the irregularities in the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls by the Election Commission (EC) in Bihar, and with a vow to prevent anyone from stealing anyone's votes.

items.headline: Mamata Leads Massive Kolkata Rally Against SIR, Vows To ‘Topple Delhi’ Over Voter List Purge
items.claim: ETV Bharat reported that Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee led a procession in Kolkata against the SIR on the day enumeration began in West Bengal. She called the SIR an assault on democratic rights.
items.quote: Kolkata: Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee led a huge procession from Dr B.R. Ambedkar’s statue to Thakurbari, Constitution in hand, joined by lakhs, including Matua and other communities, to protest the Special Intensive Revision (SIR).

items.headline: DMK, Allies Protest Against SIR Revision in Tamil Nadu
items.claim: Akashvani News reported that the DMK and its alliance partners held protest demonstrations across Tamil Nadu against the SIR, with MPs, MLAs and district functionaries taking part.
items.quote: The ruling DMK and its alliance partners are holding protest demonstrations across the State against SIR exercise.

items.headline: Mamata leads anti-SIR march; EC to meet TMC leaders on Nov 28
items.claim: The Tribune reported that Mamata Banerjee led a three-km march from Bongaon to Thakurnagar in North 24 Parganas against the SIR, after addressing a rally at Bangaon.
items.quote: West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee on Tuesday led a three-km march from Bongaon's Chandpara to Matua- heartland Thakurnagar in North 24 Parganas district to protest the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in the state.
items.response: The Tribune reported that the Commission granted a five-member TMC delegation a meeting on 28 November.

items.headline: Opposition in Assam protests 'vote theft' through SR; slams Himanta, BJP
items.claim: The Siasat Daily, carrying a PTI report, said the united opposition held a protest at Chachal in Guwahati against alleged irregularities in the draft rolls of Assam's Special Revision. Assam Congress president Gaurav Gogoi accused the state government of misusing the Election Commission.
items.quote: Guwahati : The united opposition on Friday held a protest against alleged irregularities in the draft electoral rolls and “vote theft” through the Special Revision (SR) ahead of assembly elections in Assam.
items.response: The report said the Commission stated that the flagged names had not yet been deleted and would only be processed after formal applications in the claims and objections period.

items.headline: Citizens Protest Special Intensive Revision In Bengaluru's Freedom Park
items.claim: ETV Bharat reported that trade unions, women's groups, student bodies and Dalit and minority rights groups protested against the SIR at Freedom Park in Bengaluru under the banner My Vote, My Right, and urged the state government to take a stand.
items.quote: Bengaluru: Citizens gathered at Freedom Park in Bengaluru on Saturday to protest against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR).

items.headline: Mamata Ends Dharna Against 'Flaws' In SIR
items.claim: ETV Bharat reported that Mamata Banerjee ended her sit-in against the SIR on its fifth day after the Supreme Court ordered appellate tribunals to hear appeals against exclusions in West Bengal. She said the protest was suspended temporarily.
items.quote: Kolkata: West Bengal Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee on Tuesday lifted her dharna against the "flawed SIR" on the fifth day, saying the protest was being suspended temporarily after the Supreme Court ordered the setting up of an appellate mechanism regarding the voter list revision.

items.headline: Congress Alleges Irregularities In SIR In Uttarakhand, Seeks Election Commission's Intervention
items.claim: ETV Bharat reported that a Congress delegation led by Kumari Selja staged a sit-in outside the Election Commission headquarters in Delhi over the SIR in Uttarakhand after saying it was not allowed into the premises.
items.quote: The delegation staged a sit-in outside the ECI headquarters. Later, they submitted a representation to a poll panel official, highlighting alleged discrepancies in the ongoing SIR of electoral roll in the Himalayan state.

items.headline: Congress protests against CEC Gyanesh Kumar spread across India; Gaurav Gogoi detained in Guwahati
items.claim: Business Today reported that Congress workers protested in several states demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the handling of the SIR, after The Indian Express reported objections recorded by two Election Commissioners.
items.quote: Congress workers staged protests across several parts of India on Friday, demanding the resignation and removal of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over the Election Commission’s handling of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.
items.response: Business Today reported that the Commission rejected the characterisation of these exchanges as institutional dissent and said final decisions on the SIR were unanimous.

items.headline: Congress protests against CEC Gyanesh Kumar spread across India; Gaurav Gogoi detained in Guwahati
items.claim: Business Today reported that police detained Assam Congress president and MP Gaurav Gogoi during a protest in Guwahati demanding the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation.
items.quote: In Guwahati, Assam Congress president and MP Gaurav Gogoi was detained by police while participating in a protest against Gyanesh Kumar.

items.headline: Jantar Mantar Protest Demanding Gyanesh Kumar’s Resignation Sees Mass Detentions Amid Delhi Police Crackdown
items.claim: The Quint reported that police detained protesters from civil society groups and student organisations at Jantar Mantar, among them CPI(ML) Liberation general secretary Dipankar Bhattacharya, as they demanded the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation and a rollback of the SIR.
items.quote: Several civil society groups, the All India Students’ Association, led by All India Students' Association President Neha Bora, Swaraj Party leader Yogendra Yadav, and activist Prashant Bhushan held a protest at Jantar Mantar to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and a rollback of the SIR exercise.

items.headline: Congress workers protest against CEC in Lucknow, clash with police
items.claim: ThePrint, carrying a PTI report, said police detained Uttar Pradesh Congress president Ajay Rai and hundreds of party workers in Lucknow after they were stopped while marching to demand the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation.
items.quote: Lucknow, Sep 25 (PTI) Congress workers, demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, clashed with police here on Friday after they were stopped from marching towards the Uttar Pradesh Assembly.

items.headline: 'Gyanesh, it's done bro!': Youth Congress marches to Jantar Mantar; water cannons in Bihar, Punjab
items.claim: ThePrint reported that police used water cannons on Congress workers in Patna who were protesting against the Chief Election Commissioner as part of the party's nationwide programme over the SIR.
items.quote: In Patna, Bihar, police used water cannons to disperse Congress workers protesting against Gyanesh Kumar and demanding his resignation.
items.response: ThePrint reported that the Commission said operational queries and internal feedback are part of the normal functioning of a multi-member body and that all final SIR decisions were unanimous.

items.headline: 'Gyanesh, it's done bro!': Youth Congress marches to Jantar Mantar; water cannons in Bihar, Punjab
items.claim: ThePrint reported that police used water cannons on Punjab Congress workers demonstrating in Chandigarh as part of the party's protests over the SIR.
items.quote: Similar scenes were witnessed in Punjab, where police deployed water cannons as Congress workers staged a demonstration in Chandigarh.

items.headline: HP Congress protests in Shimla; demands CEC Gyanesh Kumar's removal, arrest
items.claim: ThePrint, carrying a PTI report, said the Himachal Pradesh Congress protested outside the Election Commission office in Shimla, burned an effigy of the Chief Election Commissioner and raised slogans against the SIR.
items.quote: The Congress workers burned an effigy of Kumar, blackened the Commission’s board, and wrote “Chor Aayog” on it. They also raised slogans against the CEC and the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

items.headline: Meghalaya Cong burns Gyanesh Kumar effigy, demands his removal and arrest
items.claim: UNI reported that Congress workers in Shillong, led by state Congress president Vincent H. Pala, burned an effigy of the Chief Election Commissioner and demanded his removal amid the row over the SIR.
items.quote: Congress workers in Meghalaya burnt an effigy of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar here on Friday, demanding his immediate arrest and removal amid an ongoing row over the functioning of the Election Commission and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

items.headline: Uttarakhand Congress gheraos EC office, demands CEC's resignation
items.claim: Asianet Newsable reported that the Uttarakhand Congress marched in Dehradun, surrounded the Election Commission office and burned an effigy of the Chief Election Commissioner. The party raised concerns over how names were added and deleted and how objections were disposed of.
items.quote: The protesters marched from the Pradesh Congress office to the Secretariat, raising slogans, and later "gheraoed the Election Commission office". They also burnt an effigy of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

items.headline: Karnataka Cong protests against SIR, demands CEC Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation
items.claim: ThePrint, carrying a PTI report, said the Karnataka Congress, with Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar and former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah, protested at Freedom Park in Bengaluru against the SIR and demanded the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation.
items.quote: Bengaluru, Sep 26 (PTI) Karnataka Congress on Saturday staged a protest at Freedom Park here against the Election Commission’s SIR exercise, demanding the resignation and arrest of CEC Gyanesh Kumar.
items.response: The Election Commission, however, has asserted that its official orders, decisions and administrative directions have full legal sanction, and that differing views and observations are a normal part of deliberations within any institution.

items.headline: Gehlot, Dotasra detained during Cong protest in Jaipur over SIR row
items.claim: ThePrint, carrying a PTI report, said police used water cannons and detained former Chief Minister Ashok Gehlot and state Congress chief Govind Singh Dotasra during a march to the State Election Commission office in Jaipur over alleged SIR irregularities.
items.quote: Jaipur, Sep 28 (PTI) Former chief minister Ashok Gehlot and Rajasthan Congress chief Govind Singh Dotasra were among senior party leaders detained by police during a protest march to the State Election Commission office here on Monday over alleged vote theft and irregularities in SIR.

items.headline: Fresh protest at Jantar Mantar on October 10 if CEC Kumar didn't resign: CJP leader Dipke
items.claim: ThePrint, carrying a PTI report, said the Cockroach Janta Party held a protest at Shivaji Park in Mumbai and announced a protest at Jantar Mantar on 10 October if the Chief Election Commissioner did not resign.
items.quote: Earlier in the day, speaking at a protest organised by the CJP at Shivaji Park in Mumbai, Dipke had warned of “Jantar Mantar 2.0” if Kumar did not step down.

items.headline: ‘Attempt to kill democracy’: Hyderabad civil society protests SIR, demands CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation
items.claim: The South First reported that more than a dozen civil society groups held a day-long protest at Dharna Chowk in Hyderabad, demanding that the SIR be scrapped and the Chief Election Commissioner resign.
items.quote: Citizens in Hyderabad gathered at Dharna Chowk on Saturday, 3 October, for a day-long protest against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

items.headline: Garjana Morcha: Uddhav, Raj Thackeray Lead Protest Seeking Gyanesh Kumar’s Resignation, Scrapping Of Maharashtra SIR
items.claim: The Free Press Journal reported that Uddhav Thackeray of the Shiv Sena (UBT) and Raj Thackeray of the MNS led the Virat Garjana Morcha in Mumbai, demanding that the SIR in Maharashtra be cancelled and the Chief Election Commissioner resign.
items.quote: Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray and Maharashtra Navnirman Sena chief Raj Thackeray on Sunday led a protest seeking the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over allegations of irregularities in the special intensive revision process.

items.headline: Delhi Police Detain Rahul, Priyanka Gandhi During INDIA Bloc Protest Seeking CEC's Resignation
items.claim: The Wire reported that police stopped an INDIA bloc march from Parliament to the Election Commission, and that opposition MPs held a sit-in at the All India Radio building until police detained Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra that night.
items.quote: As night fell on Tuesday, October 6, opposition parties had refused to vacate the protest site until they were allowed to meet Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and hand over their demand for his resignation.

items.headline: AAP Protest: Delhi CEO office gheraoed over SIR, CEC resignation demanded
items.claim: Deccan Herald, carrying a PTI report, said AAP workers and members of other parties protested outside the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer's office demanding the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation over alleged SIR irregularities. It said AAP had earlier protested at Jantar Mantar and India Gate.
items.quote: New Delhi: Scores of AAP and other parties' workers protested outside the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer's office at Kashmere Gate on Wednesday for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

items.headline: INDIA bloc leaders march to EC office in Delhi, seek rollback of SIR
items.claim: The Tribune reported that Delhi leaders of the INDIA bloc marched to the Election Commission office and gave the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer a memorandum demanding that the SIR be cancelled and excluded eligible voters be restored. It said police detained Delhi Congress president Devender Yadav at a separate protest at Jantar Mantar.
items.quote: Delhi leaders of the INDIA bloc on Wednesday staged a protest march from Kashmiri Gate to the Election Commission (EC) office and submitted a memorandum to the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer, demanding immediate cancellation of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and restoration of names of eligible voters excluded from the draft rolls.

items.headline: Kerala BLO death sparks boycott; BLOs strike over SIR deadline stress
items.claim: The News Minute reported that hundreds of booth level officers across Kerala stayed away from SIR work on a strike call after the death of a BLO in Kannur, and that employee and teacher action councils marched to collectorates.
items.quote: A day after the death of a Booth Level Officer in Kerala’s Kannur, allegedly due Special Intensive Revision (SIR) workpressure, hundreds of Booth Level Officers (BLOs) across the state skipped work following a strike call on Monday, November 17.
items.response: The News Minute reported that Kerala's Chief Electoral Officer said he had not received any complaints regarding work pressure from BLOs.

items.headline: Tamil Nadu revenue employees association begin boycott of SIR work
items.claim: Deccan Herald, carrying a PTI report, said the Federation of Revenue Associations of Tamil Nadu began a statewide boycott of SIR work over workload, staff shortages, deadline pressure and poor training.
items.quote: Chennai: The members of the Federation of Revenue Associations of Tamil Nadu commenced their boycott of the SIR work from Tuesday, protesting against excessive workload, insufficient manpower, deadline pressure, and inadequate training.

items.headline: BLOs protest outside Bengal CEO's office over excessive work pressure, EC calls them 'real heroes'
items.claim: Deccan Herald, carrying a PTI report, said booth level officers marching under the BLO Adhikar Raksha Committee clashed with police outside the West Bengal Chief Electoral Officer's office in Kolkata over SIR workload.
items.quote: Kolkata: Alleging "excessive work pressure" and "unmanageable workload", Booth-level officers (BLOs) engaged in the ongoing SIR process in West Bengal clashed with the police on Monday while attempting to enter the Chief Electoral Officer's (CEO) office here during a demonstration, a senior officer said.
items.response: Deccan Herald reported that Chief Electoral Officer Manoj Agarwal described the BLOs as the "real heroes" of the exercise.

items.headline: Ahmedabad: 250 BLOs Stage Protest, Citing Threats, Pressure, Abuse and Late Night Calls
items.claim: The Wire reported that nearly 250 primary school teachers working as booth level officers stopped work and held a sit-in at a data uploading centre in Ahmedabad, alleging threats and pressure during the SIR.
items.quote: Nearly 250 primary school teachers assigned as Booth Level Officers (BLOs) halted work and held a sit-in protest on Thursday (November 27) at the data uploading centre in Khokhra, Ahmedabad, alleging “threat and pressure” during the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

items.headline: Up:blo की मौतों से नाराज शिक्षकों संगठनों ने खोला मोर्चा
items.claim: Amar Ujala reported that teachers' organisations in Uttar Pradesh, among them the Uttar Pradeshiya Prathmik Shikshak Sangh, objected to the deaths of teachers and staff on SIR duty and demanded jobs and compensation for their families.
items.quote: प्रदेश में विशेष गहन पुनरीक्षण अभियान में लगे शिक्षामित्रों व कर्मचारियों की मौत से शिक्षक संगठनों में काफी नाराजगी है। उनका कहना है कि उनका काम शिक्षण कार्य है, उसके बावजूद प्रशासन जबरन उनसे निर्वाचन से जुड़े कार्य कराता है।

items.headline: ‘EC Played Like a Puppet’: INDIA Bloc Seals Roadmap to Ramp Up Anti-SIR Agitation
items.claim: Leaders of the INDIA bloc, 33 of them from 19 parties, agreed a plan of district marches from 2 to 8 October, a march of opposition MPs to the Commission on 6 October, a meeting with the President in the second week of October and five rallies including one in Delhi on 1 November, The Wire reported. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said the Commission was being used as a puppet by the Prime Minister and the Home Minister.
items.quote: The leaders' six-point action plan included "Save Democracy" marches at the district level from October 2-8, opposition MPs march to the Election Commission on October 6, a meeting with the President in the second week of October, five major rallies by the opposition including a major rally in New Delhi on November 1 as well as an appeal for the early resolution of all cases relating to the SIR and electoral matters pending before the Supreme Court.

items.headline: CEC row | EC refuses Opposition's demand for meeting
items.claim: Opposition MPs of the INDIA bloc marched from Parliament to the Commission's headquarters to press for the Chief Election Commissioner's removal, and asked for 240 MPs to meet the three Commissioners at Parliament House Annexe, Deccan Herald reported.
items.quote: "After 4.00 PM today, when the Election Commission was considering the above proposal for the...meeting with the...MPs, it was informed by the Deputy Commissioner of Police, Delhi Police, that the meeting being sought was to be held with a group of 240 MPs and that the proposed venue was the Parliament House Annexe," the EC said in a statement. The EC considered this request as "unusual and therefore, could not be accepted," as, in accordance with the protocol, such meetings are held only on the premises of the poll body. It then proposed that its "senior-most officer on duty could be sent to the meeting venue to receive the memorandum", which in itself would have been an "unprecedented step". The statement added, "however, this offer was also declined by the MPs."
items.response: The Commission said no party had sought an appointment until 4 pm, that a meeting of 240 MPs away from its premises was unusual and could not be accepted, and that the MPs declined its offer to send its senior-most officer on duty to receive their memorandum, Deccan Herald reported.
items.note: Deccan Herald published 7 Oct 2026 00:01 IST about the events of 6 Oct. Asianet Newsable carries the ANI copy (6 Oct, 10 PM) with fuller text of the statement, and agrees. ThePrint's PTI copy (theprint.in/.../3063760/) exists but is behind a bot check.

items.headline: Cockroach Janta Party protest: New Delhi sealed even before the first slogan
items.claim: The South First reported that police stopped the Cockroach Janta Party's protest at Jantar Mantar demanding the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation over the SIR, and detained CPI(M) leaders.
items.quote: "A gathering of more than four people is not allowed," a Delhi Police officer told CPM's Rajya Sabha MP John Brittas, when he tried to argue that there were only three of them. ... "This is a murder of democracy," Pinarayi told reporters.
items.response: No statement from the Commission was reported. Police told the protesters that a gathering of more than four people was not allowed.
items.note: Mid-morning report of 10 October. Detention counts conflict between sources (Delhi Police about 500 at 9.45 am per ThePrint's live blog). How the day ended was not found in any opened source. The page names a YouTuber and other CJP members, who are left out.

items.headline: INDIA bloc hands over memorandum on 'vote chori' to President Murmu, says she didn't deny charge
items.claim: An INDIA bloc delegation including Mallikarjun Kharge and Rahul Gandhi gave President Droupadi Murmu a memorandum after opposition MPs marched from Parliament House and were stopped by police at Vijay Chowk, PTI reported. Kharge said the President had asked for evidence, which the bloc would provide, and Rahul Gandhi said she had not denied what they told her and that the leaders would meet the Chief Justice on Monday. The News Mill reported that the memorandum asked for the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation, repeal of the 2023 law on the Commissioners, suspension of the SIR with the names the bloc says were left off or deleted illegally put back, a return to paper ballots, and annulment of Assembly elections of the past two years where it said evidence of vote theft had been presented. These are the INDIA bloc's demands and allegations.
items.quote: "President in no way denied what we said, she did not question what we said... she accepted our statement and sought proof of 'election chori',"
items.response: No response from Rashtrapati Bhavan or the Commission to the memorandum was reported.
items.note: One item for the meeting and its memorandum, from two reports. The News Mill calls it a four-point memorandum but lists five demands, and expands SIR wrongly as 'Systematic Internal Review'. The memorandum's text was not found. The bloc's figure of 13.3 crore voters removed is its own and is left out of the claim.

items.headline: Punjab House resolution seeks probe into electoral ‘irregularities’ under CEC Gyanesh Kumar
items.claim: The Punjab Vidhan Sabha passed a resolution by voice vote on 23 October asking for an independent and impartial inquiry into alleged irregularities in voter lists, the electoral process and the functioning of the Election Commission under the Chief Election Commissioner, The Indian Express reported. The paper calls it the first resolution of its kind by an Assembly against the Chief Election Commissioner. Members of the Congress, the Shiromani Akali Dal and the BJP were not in the House when it passed. These are the resolution's and the speakers' allegations.
items.quote: This House demands establishment of an independent, impartial, and credible investigative mechanism to inquire into alleged irregularities concerning the electoral process and voter lists under Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, so that the truth can come to light and accountability can be fixed,
items.response: The report carries no response from the Commission or the BJP.
items.note: By Kanchan Vasdev, published 23 October 2026, 8:37 pm IST, read in full from the page's JSON-LD articleBody with curl on 24 October 2026. Tabled by Finance Minister Harpal Singh Cheema. Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann's claim in the debate that 14 crore names were deleted nationwide is his, and is not carried here. Punjab's own revision is over, and the site's data gives its final roll as 12 October 2026.

items.headline: Over 150 detained in Delhi during protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar
items.claim: Delhi Police detained more than 150 people on 23 October at a march in central Delhi against the revision and the Chief Election Commissioner, called by the Delhi Coordination Committee of People Against SIR, The Indian Express reported. About 300 people gathered near Gole Dak Khana around 2 pm and marched towards Gurdwara Bangla Sahib. When they could not reach the Commission's office they held a sit-in near the roundabout, and security forces began detaining them by 3 pm. The paper also reported that over 57 cases registered during the protests of 2 to 15 October had been moved to the Crime Branch.
items.quote: Delhi Police Friday detained more than 150 protesters during a march in Central Delhi against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
items.response: A senior police officer said the cases were moved because they needed close technical investigation and thorough questioning.
items.note: By Pragynesh, published 23 October 2026, 5:10 pm IST, read in full from the page's JSON-LD articleBody with curl on 24 October 2026. The march is the People's March of 23 October on the Events page. The report names party leaders and invitees, who are public figures.

items.headline: Students, youth activists arrested for protesting against SIR in Chennai
items.claim: Chennai police arrested students and youth activists who began a 24-hour sit-in against the revision near Rajarathinam Stadium in Egmore at 4 pm on 22 October in defiance of a police ban, The Hindu reported. Nine organisations, among them Left student and youth groups and the Cockroach Janta Party, had formed a platform called Chennai's Jantar Mantar 2.0 and asked for the Chief Election Commissioner's resignation. They were held overnight at a community hall and released the next morning at the stadium, where they resumed the protest.
items.quote: The city police on Thursday arrested students and youth activists who launched a 24-hour protest against the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in defiance of a police ban.
items.response: The report carries no statement from the police beyond the ban.
items.note: The Hindu Bureau, published 24 October 2026, 12:55 am IST, read in full from the page's JSON-LD articleBody with curl on 24 October 2026. The report says Thursday, which was 22 October. Listed on People Against SIR's map for 22 October.

items.headline: Keralam SIR: LDF representatives walk out of all-party meet convened by Chief Electoral Officer
items.claim: Representatives of the Left Democratic Front walked out of an all-party meeting called by Kerala's Chief Electoral Officer on 23 October for the Special Summary Revision, The Hindu reported, and asked that the names of 24.08 lakh voters left off the draft roll of the state's earlier revision be put back. The paper reports that 24.08 lakh is the fall at the draft stage and that the final roll of 21 February 2026 was 8.97 lakh below the roll of October 2025.
items.quote: The CEO expressed his helplessness. We have asked the CEO to convey the demand to the Election Commission of India (ECI),
items.response: The Chief Electoral Officer, D. Sajith Babu, said he had told the leaders he would convey to the Commission their demand that the 2 November deadline for rationalising polling stations be extended.
items.note: The Hindu Bureau, published 23 October 2026, 4:40 pm IST, read in full from the page's JSON-LD articleBody with curl on 24 October 2026. The quote is CPI(M) leader M.V. Jayarajan's. The paper's figures match the site's Kerala data (frozen roll 2,78,50,855, draft 2,54,42,352, final 2,69,53,644).

items.case: Uday Bhanu Chib v. Union of India and Ors, Delhi High Court
items.headline: Decision to de-notify Jantar Mantar as protest site taken after Supreme Court order: Delhi police to High Court
items.claim: The Delhi Police told the Delhi High Court on 13 October that it de-notified Jantar Mantar as the designated protest site, and identified three other sites, on the basis of the Supreme Court's order of 9 October, Bar and Bench reported. That order had said suitable sites where basic amenities could be provided to protesters should be identified, and left the decision to the competent authority. The submission came on Indian Youth Congress president Uday Bhanu Chib's petition against the refusal of permission to protest at Jantar Mantar against the Chief Election Commissioner. Justice Amit Mahajan issued notice on three of its prayers, which challenge the police's reliance on its 2022 standing order and the 10-day advance notice for protests.
items.quote: The Court said appropriate sites need to be identified and designated and we have precisely done that,
items.response: The police said the petition had become infructuous because Jantar Mantar had been de-notified. On 15 October the Solicitor General told the Supreme Court that the decision followed the recommendations of a committee set up by the Union Home Ministry well before the Court's oral observations, Bar and Bench reported.
items.note: Bar and Bench, by Prashant Jha, published 13 October 2026, 6:20 pm IST (modified 14 October). The Supreme Court's hearing of 15 October on a separate challenge to the de-notification: Bar and Bench, by Ritwik Choudhury, 15 October 2026. Both read in full from the JSON-LD articleBody with curl on 24 October 2026. The quote is Additional Solicitor General Chetan Sharma's. The petitioner is a party office-holder. The Supreme Court order of 9 October is the one on Metro and train closures (court-36). The two accounts of why Jantar Mantar was de-notified differ, and both are given.

items.case: Petition by the Delhi Kirana Committee and the Delhi Iron and Hardware Merchant Association, Supreme Court
items.headline: 'If NDMC Order Disproportionate, We'll Act': Supreme Court Lists Petition Against CJP Protest After Vacation
items.claim: Counsel for two traders' associations raised in the Supreme Court on 16 October their petition against the Cockroach Janta Party's call to unfurl the tricolour in Connaught Place's Central Park that evening, saying it would obstruct trade worth Rs 200 crore a day, The Wire reported. The party had called the protest after two of its leaders were arrested for waving the flag at Jantar Mantar. The bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi said it would act on compensation if the NDMC's restrictions were found disproportionate, noted that the Delhi High Court was hearing a similar matter, and listed the petition for 26 and 27 October, after the Dussehra break.
items.quote: If we feel that the NDMC’s order is a disproportionate restriction, we told you, there is ample jurisdiction evolved by this court under compensation and public law. We will act
items.response: The Wire says the petitions appear to be concerned with the protest itself, though counsel told the Court the NDMC had shut the place by a notice the night before, as LiveLaw reported. It carries the party founder's post on X that businesses suffer when the government shuts down a city and restricts its citizens' movement.
items.note: The Wire Staff, published 16 October 2026, 2:01 pm IST, citing LiveLaw, read in full through The Wire's CMS API on 24 October 2026. The quote is Justice Bagchi's. Advocate Jai Anant Dehadrai mentioned the petition. The report calls the NDMC the New Delhi Municipal Corporation. The two arrested leaders and the party's founder are named in the report and are given here by role. The Delhi High Court matter is the one in which, the report says, the police said a day earlier that they would take all possible measures to control the protest.

items.case: A teacher's petition against his suspension from booth level officer duty, Punjab and Haryana High Court
items.headline: Punjab & Haryana High Court grants relief to teacher suspended for not joining SIR duty after wife's death
items.claim: The Punjab and Haryana High Court quashed the suspension of a teacher in Hisar district who had asked to be relieved of booth level officer duty after his wife died, and imposed costs of Rs 50,000 on the District Elementary Education Officer, Hisar and the Electoral Registration Officer for the Barwala constituency, Bar and Bench reported. Justice Harpreet Singh Brar found that the authorities appointed three substitutes for his booth without making sure any of them joined, and then suspended him for a duty he no longer held. The Court directed the Chief Electoral Officer, Haryana to make sure that a booth level officer who is replaced is told in writing whether he stands relieved.
items.quote: Instead of deciding his application, the respondents appointed one substitute after another without ensuring that any of them actually joined. They then held the petitioner responsible for the default of others, replaced him, and thereafter suspended him for a duty he no longer held, on an allegation of missing a training whose date they themselves cannot state
items.response: The authorities said he had never been relieved of the duty and had missed the SIR training. The Court found they could not state the date of the training, and noted that none of the three substitutes attended it either.
items.note: Bar and Bench (staff byline), published 17 October 2026, 11:50 am IST (modified 19 October), read in full from the JSON-LD articleBody with curl on 24 October 2026. The report says the order was passed recently and does not date it, so the date is the publication date. The teacher is named in the case title and the report, and is a private person, so he is not named. He was suspended on 7 July 2026 and had been without salary from 2 June. The Court directed his dues to be cleared within four weeks.

items.headline: 'Hold Civic Polls Only After Deleted Voters Return to Rolls': Mamata TMC, Left, Congress, Rights Groups Urge EC
items.claim: The Congress, the Trinamool Congress, the CPI(M), the CPI(ML) Liberation, civil rights organisations and public figures gave West Bengal's State Election Commissioner a memorandum on 26 October asking that elections to the Kolkata and Howrah municipal corporations be held only after electors deleted in the revision have been heard, The Wire reported. They asked the State Election Commission to use its powers under Section 5 of the West Bengal State Election Commission Act, 1994 to add to the civic rolls everyone whose appeal is pending before the SIR appellate tribunals. Citing the Election Commission's affidavit of 16 September in the Supreme Court, the memorandum puts the pending appeals at about 1.2 lakh in the Kolkata Municipal Corporation area and about 39,000 in the Howrah Municipal Corporation area. It asks that the polls wait until the re-enrolment drive and the Special Summary Revision, whose final roll is due on 4 January 2027, are complete.
items.quote: Excluding around 1.6 lakh appellants in the two corporations from the civic rolls “would disenfranchise them for the second time, after the assembly polls,” the memorandum said.
items.response: The State Election Commissioner's office said he would meet a delegation of the signatories on 28 October, according to their press release as The Wire reports it. No reply from the State Election Commission on the substance was reported.
items.note: The Wire (The Wire Staff), published 27 October 2026, 11:40 am IST, read in full through The Wire's API with curl on 27 October 2026. The signatories named in the report include the West Bengal Pradesh Congress Committee president Subhankar Sarkar, Trinamool Congress MP Sougata Roy, CPI(M) state committee member Samik Lahiri, CPI(ML) Liberation politburo member Partha Ghosh and former Rajya Sabha MP Jawhar Sircar, with members of civil society groups who are not named here. The memorandum says that, by the Commission's data, all the tribunal cases decided in Kolkata district and 99% in Howrah went in favour of inclusion. The figures are the memorandum's, citing the Commission's affidavit, and were not checked against the affidavit.
